posts.planGate: Metricool Free plan: schedule only after Rej has confirmed the Starter upgrade in chat
altText: Navy slide with Educate Me AI logo. Text: AQA or Edexcel? Same two days, different papers. English Literature 2027: dates, lengths and what sits where. Save this.
Two date cards: Paper 1, Wednesday 12 May, morning. Paper 2, Wednesday 19 May, morning. AQA and Edexcel sit English Literature on the same days. On OCR or Eduqas, check your board's own timetable.

What's in each paper? AQA Paper 1, Shakespeare and the 19th-century novel: 1 hour 45 minutes, 40 percent. AQA Paper 2, Modern texts and poetry: 2 hours 15 minutes, 60 percent. Edexcel Paper 1, Shakespeare and post-1914 literature: 1 hour 45 minutes, 50 percent. Edexcel Paper 2, 19th-century novel and poetry since 1789: 2 hours 15 minutes, 50 percent.

What this means for revision. The 19th-century novel is on Paper 1 for AQA but Paper 2 for Edexcel, so write down which text is on which paper. AQA Paper 2 is 60 percent of the grade; Edexcel's two papers are worth the same. Do a timed answer on each paper's question types before Christmas.

posts.title: Up 10%, then down 10%. Back where you started?
posts.planGate: Metricool Free plan: schedule only after Rej has confirmed the Starter upgrade in chat
altText: Reel, Lock It In number 2, GCSE Maths, Percentages. Question: up 10%, then down 10%. Back where you started? A bar fills from £100 on the left to £99 on the right, with two labels: Up 10% (£10): £110, then Down 10% of £110 (£11): £99. A note says it is not £100, it is 1% lower. Text: Up 10% means times 1.1. Down 10% means times 0.9. 1.1 times 0.9 equals 0.99, so you finish on 99% of the start. The second 10% is taken from the new, bigger amount. Memory trick: percent of what? Each change uses the latest amount, so the two don't cancel out. Ends on: Save this. Lock it in. Follow for Lock It In number 3.

Memory trick: percent of what? Each change uses the latest amount, so the two don’t cancel out.

posts.title: IGCSE or GCSE? Check which one you’re revising for
posts.planGate: Metricool Free plan: schedule only after Rej has confirmed the Starter upgrade in chat
altText: Navy slide with Educate Me AI logo. Text: IGCSE or GCSE? Check which one you're revising for. Exam sessions are one thing that can differ. Save this.

When can you sit the exams? Two examples, always check your own board. GCSE in England: main exams in May and June. GCSE English Language and Maths also have a November session, for students aged 16 or over on 31 August of that year. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE: May and June, and November for selected subjects. Pearson stopped its January International GCSE series after January 2023.

How to check which you're taking. Look at the qualification name: your school's entry or timetable says GCSE or International GCSE, and names the board. Look at the exam board: each board and subject has its own specification, so revise from yours. Ask your school which sessions you're entered for, and when the timetable comes out.

IGCSE or GCSE? They are different qualifications, so check which one you’re revising for. One thing that can differ is when you can sit the exams.

GCSEs in England are mainly sat in May/June. GCSE English Language and Maths also have a November session, for students aged 16 or over on 31 August of that year. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is offered in May/June, and November for selected subjects; its January session ended after January 2023.

Your school’s entry and your exam board’s own timetable are what count. Save this, and send it to a friend or parent. Join early access · link in bio.
